text: You're a salt miner thirteen hundred feet under a lake in Louisiana, on November twentieth, nineteen eighty.
Right above you, Texaco is drilling for oil from a rig in the middle of the lake.
But somebody got the math wrong, and the drill is headed straight for your mine.
At twelve hundred feet, it punches through the ceiling, and the rig up top starts to tip.
The crew gets off just in time, and the whole rig rolls over and sinks.
Down here, the lake starts pouring in, and the elevator only fits eight men at a time.
Up top, the lake turns into a whirlpool a quarter mile wide. It swallows two rigs, a tugboat, eleven barges and part of an island.
In three hours, the whole lake is gone.
Then the canal to the Gulf starts running backward, and makes the tallest waterfall Louisiana has ever had.
A few days later, most of the barges pop back up, like corks.
Every single miner made it out alive, and the ten foot lake is now two hundred feet deep.
Share this with someone who would panic in that elevator, and subscribe for more true stories.
